title: How a drop works in Puck
question: When you drag a block onto a Puck page and let go, what changes, and when?
intro: Puck is a drag-and-drop page editor for React. This page follows one drag: a Heading block from the component list, dropped between two blocks already on the page. It starts zoomed out and ends on single lines of code.
subject: Puck 0.23.0 · packages/core · commit 574471f5

terms.root:default-zone: Puck's name for the page's main list of blocks. The part before the colon is the owner (root, the page itself). The part after is the list's name.
terms.insertComponent: Puck's function that adds a new block to the page.
terms.appStore: Puck's page data store: the place in memory that holds your page and tells the screen when it changes.
terms.getState: A function on the store. Calling it returns what the store holds at that moment.
terms.insertAction: The function that works out the new page data for an "add a block" action.
terms.||: JavaScript's "or". It uses the left value if there is one, otherwise the right one.
terms.defaultProps: The starting settings you gave a block in your Puck setup.
terms.populateIds: A helper that gives ids to any blocks nested inside the new block.
terms.root: Puck's id for the page itself.
terms.Columns-abc:left: An example drop area name: the left column of a Columns block whose id is Columns-abc.
terms.walkAppState: A helper that builds new page data by visiting every list and every block.
terms.insert: A tiny helper that returns a copy of a list with one item added.
terms.result.splice(1, 0, item): Insert item at position 1 and remove nothing. Positions start at 0.
terms.splice(1, 0, item): Insert item at position 1 and remove nothing. Positions start at 0.
terms.insertedState: A copy of the new page data, kept only inside insertComponent.
terms.dispatch: The store's function for receiving an action. Sending an action is the only way the page data changes.
terms.recordHistory: true: A setting on the action that tells Puck to save an undo step for this change.
terms.onAction: An optional function your app can give Puck. Puck calls it after every action.
terms.itemSelector: Puck's address for one block: which drop area, and which position in it.
terms.resolveData: An optional function in a block's setup that can load or change its data, for example from a server.

sections.title: Words you need first
sections.intro: Five words come up on every step. Each card says what the word means in plain terms.

items.meaning: One piece of a page, like a Heading or a Text block. You write each block as a React component.
A list on the page that you can drop blocks into. The page has one. A Columns block has one per column.
items.example: Puck names each one owner:list. The page's main list is root:default-zone.

items.meaning: A place in memory that holds data and tells the screen when the data changes. Puck has two stores.
The temporary store. It holds what you are dragging and where it would land. It changes many times a second.
The store that holds your real page: which blocks, in what order, with what settings.
A small note that describes one change, like "add a Heading at position 1". You send it to the page data store, and the store applies it.

sections.title: Puck, from far away
sections.intro: The map starts with the six areas of the editor. Click an area to see its parts, or press Next to follow one drag.

start.title: Your page changes once: on drop
body: While you drag, Puck writes only to the temporary drag store. The canvas draws a line where the block would land.
Your real page, in the page data store, changes once, when you let go.

areas.name: The Puck editor
areas.about: The component you put in your app. It creates both stores and holds everything below.

areas.name: Canvas
areas.about: Your page, inside an iframe (a page inside the page)

areas.name: Drag handling
areas.about: dnd-kit plus Puck's own code. Together they decide where a drop lands.

areas.name: Data
areas.about: A temporary store for drags, and a store for your real page

parts.name: Component list
parts.about: The list of blocks you can add, like Heading or Text. You can drag from it, but you can't drop onto it.

parts.name: Outline
parts.about: A list of every block on your page. You can drag a block to a new spot in this list. When you let go, Puck moves the block on the page too.

parts.name: Drop area
parts.about: A list on the page that you can drop blocks into. It redraws when you add, remove or move a block in it, and when its drag preview changes.

parts.name: Drag wrapper
parts.about: Puck wraps every block on the page in this. It lets you drag the block. When you drag another block over it, it decides whether that block goes before it or after it.

parts.name: Drop line
parts.about: The thin blue line that shows where the block will land. It only appears while you drag.

parts.name: Fields panel
parts.about: Shows the settings of the selected block. When you type, it saves the change to the page data store.

parts.name: dnd-kit
parts.about: A free drag-and-drop library. It waits until you hold for 200 milliseconds or move 5 pixels, so a click isn't taken as a drag. Then it tells Puck what the block is over.

parts.name: Drag handler
parts.about: Puck's main drag code. On every pointer move it works out the drop area and position, and writes them to the drag store. When you drop, it saves to the page data once.

parts.name: Area finder
parts.about: An add-on Puck plugs into dnd-kit. Drop areas can sit inside each other. Every 50 milliseconds it picks the innermost drop area under the pointer that allows the block you are dragging.

parts.name: Drag store
parts.about: The temporary store. It holds what you are dragging and where it would land. Your page data isn't touched.

parts.name: Page data store
parts.about: Holds your real page and which block you selected. It changes only when it receives an action.

links.label: signs up as a drop spot

areaLinks.label: preview while dragging, save on drop

tour.say: Follow one drag. Press Next to drag a Heading from the component list onto the page. Watch which parts light up.
You press on Heading in the component list. dnd-kit waits until you hold for 200 milliseconds or move 5 pixels. Then it starts a drag.
As you move, the area finder asks the browser what is under the pointer. It writes the innermost drop area that allows a Heading into the drag store.
dnd-kit checks the blocks in that drop area. The pointer is over the Text block, so it tells Puck's drag handler.
The drag handler works out the position: 1, between Hero and Text. It writes that to the drag store as a preview. Your page data has not changed.
The drop area sees its new preview and draws the blue drop line. Steps 2 to 5 repeat on every pointer move.
You let go. The Heading glides into place. Then the drag handler sends one action to the page data store: add a Heading at position 1.
The page's main list changed, so only that drop area redraws. React adds the Heading to the canvas.

steps.say: The dropped block has finished gliding, and the blue line is gone. The drag handler calls insertComponent. It passes the type Heading, the drop area root:default-zone and position 1.

log.text: Glide finished. Calling insertComponent: Heading, main list, position 1.

steps.say: appStore is the page data store. This line takes out its getState function, which returns what the store holds right now.
Make the block's permanent id: its type plus a random string. Puck throws away the temporary id it used during the drag.
Write the change down as a plain object. Puck calls this an action: a note that says what should happen. Nothing has changed yet.

vars.stateBefore: page data · main list: Hero-1, Text-2

steps.say: Read the current page data. The page's main list has two blocks: Hero and Text.

vars.stateBefore: page data · main list: Hero-1, Text-2

steps.say: Call insertAction. That function works out the new page data for an "add a block" action. Press Next to step inside it.
We are inside insertAction now. The action already has an id, so this line reuses it. The part after || would make a new id only if one were missing.
Build the new block: its type, its starting settings from your setup (defaultProps), and its id. populateIds gives ids to blocks nested inside it. A Heading has none.
Puck names every drop area owner:list. Splitting root:default-zone at the colon gives the owner: root, the page itself. A column could be Columns-abc:left.
Puck keeps a lookup table of every block by id, to find any block quickly. This line lists the blocks the owner sits inside. The page sits inside nothing, so the list is empty.
walkAppState builds new page data without editing the old. It runs the first function below on every list, then the second on every block.
The walk reaches the page's main list. Its name matches the drop area we want, so this list gets the Heading.
Now we are in insert. It copies the list first and never edits the old one. React spots a change by seeing a new list.

ask.q: The next line is result.splice(1, 0, item). Where does the Heading land?
ask.why: splice(1, 0, item) means: go to position 1, remove nothing, insert the item. Positions start at 0, so position 1 is right after Hero.

steps.say: This one line is the whole drop. The list is now Hero, Heading, Text. Everything before it worked out the position. Everything after it saves the change and shows it.

log.text: Added the Heading to a copy of the list: Hero, Heading, Text.

steps.say: Hand back the new list. It has three blocks, but only in the new copy. The page data store still holds the old list.

This function runs once per block. It decides whether Puck updates that block's lookup table entry. Returning null means leave it alone. All three blocks are in the changed list, so Puck updates all three.

steps.say: Back in insertComponent. insertedState holds complete new page data, with the Heading in it.

ask.q: insertedState has the Heading in it. Is the Heading on the screen now?
ask.why: No. insertedState is only a value inside this function. The store has not changed, so nothing redraws. Check the saved data panel: still two blocks.

steps.say: Send the same action to the store, for real. recordHistory: true means undo can remove it.
We are inside the store. It runs the function that applies actions. For an "insert" action, that calls insertAction again, this time on the real data.

takeaway: While you drag, Puck only updates a temporary preview. Your page data changes once, when you let go, through one line that adds the block to a list.
